I've been playing with ipfs and it is way more simple than anyone has let on. Basically it works as a free cdn that is more than happy to do video for most users and optionally with the use of an addon is a peer to peer distribution of static files for users who want to do that.

All you do is add a file with ipfs add [the file], then direct people to a gateway like venus.i.ipfs.io plus a hash. It will serve your file as long as people request it and when people don't it will ask for the file over ipfs from you once they do again (once in a blue moon).

People who want to reduce load on the gateway can run an addon that will swap the domain you give as a gateway for localhost. It doesn't really impact you whether they do or not except that theoretically you could even delete the files on the server because they would have copies but you probably wouldn't do that.

But people who wanted to run the statics of the site peer to peer could.
The easiest way to make voat distributed, reduce load, and drop cloudflare is ipfs

The similarities between ipfs and freenet are many. Freenet has you exchange blocks over proxy over proxy over proxy. ipfs has a dns like system where you can request a list of who has what resource and then get it from them directly. A middle ground would be nice.

I would only suggest using it directly if you are like me with a vpn or don't really have anything to be embarrassed about. But the main benefits are not from people using it that way. It's from relatively few doing it and the rest using a gateway.
